PAGE_ACCESS_DENIED_ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.ROOT_CAUSE: PAGE OWNERSHIP. The token in data/telegraph.json belongs to a LATER Telegraph account than the one that created the 64 pre-existing articles. Telegraph ties edit rights to the creating token.
PAGE_ACCESS_DENIED_ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.implication: no formatting change, no new token and no credential rotation can ever fix those pages. The only route is the original creating token, which exists only in the founder's browser session.
PAGE_ACCESS_DENIED_ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.no_new_token_created: confirmed - the spare probe token from cycle 114 was deleted the same cycle. Creating another token would have changed nothing, since the current token already has full write access to everything it is entitled to.
PAGE_ACCESS_DENIED_ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.token_handling: no token value was printed, logged, committed or transmitted at any point. Verification used the local data/telegraph.json only.

COMMERCIAL_WORK_CONTINUED_WITHOUT_TELEGR.principle_applied: Telegraph was treated as one channel among several, not as a gate on selling.

found_a_better_channel.why_it_is_better_right_now: Telegraph strips anchor nodes, so a product link there is plain text that must be hand-copied. Nostr carries the URL as a bare string that clients render and auto-link, so the Gumroad link survives as text a reader can tap or copy without editing Telegraph.
found_a_better_channel.precedent: existing nostr_post.py in this repo already had real relay acknowledgements (relay.damus.io, relay.primal.net, nos.lol), so this is a proven path, not a new integration.
